claude-bridge/claude-fable-5.character: Advisory: The advisor's own session model. The advisor session runs at medium. Shares the Anthropic session allowance — generally avoid assigning checking, review, reduction, browser verification, implementation, or planner nodes. Planner in this profile is Sol. When Anthropic capacity is reached, the advisor session switches to Sol at high. Grok is not in this map; use grok-cycle when Grok should own the hefty maker+review loop.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.character: Advisory: Planner by default, and the hard-implementation workhorse: long or difficult backend, data, service, mixed-stack, and genuinely hard debugging. Also the advisor-session fallback when Fable is at Anthropic capacity. Use medium for token-efficient adversarial schema/auth/security/money/final whole-diff review and hefty reduction. Use high for planning and substantial builds; escalate to xhigh or max only for genuinely difficult debugging. Generally avoid assigning scouting, browser verification, or short-leash chores — those are Luna or Sonnet. Frontend: hard or unfamiliar UX may use Sol with frontend-design loaded; medium well-known UX is Sonnet; tiny tweaks are Luna.

claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-5.character: Advisory: Cheap enough to spend in this profile: medium well-known implementation that still needs material judgment, scouting when Luna is a poor fit, reduction, and review that is not adversarial-tier. Bounded Anthropic 5-hour bursts. Load frontend-design for UX work. Generally avoid assigning planning, genuinely hard or unfamiliar implementation (that is Sol high), adversarial schema/auth/security/money/final whole-diff review (that is Sol medium), or locked execution packets (those are Luna). Grok is not a fallback here — switch to grok-cycle instead.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna.character: Advisory: Extremely cheap Codex leftover: the preferred executor for a locked execution packet, plus scouting, mechanical chores, routine mid-phase checks, repair verification, test-harness findings, and browser verification. The packet fixes material decisions, bounds the surface, and names deterministic anchors. Luna owns ordinary local code choices but stops and escalates rather than deciding product, architecture, schema, migration, auth, fallback, destructive behavior, or external effects. 272K window. Generally avoid planning, hard or decision-bearing implementation, and adversarial-tier checking. Recommended reasoning is max.
